summary: Re-derive historical cancelled-ask and attribution-only receipt projections so replicas with identical claims no longer retain different ready states or receipt facts.

replay.detail: Persistent store open once refolds run parts containing cancelled person asks (whole trees only when the existing ownership rules require it), and upgrades resource_observations from version 2 to 3 with the existing resource/preparation rebuild. Local timestamp normalization now ignores the same obsolete cancellation-derived state effects as replay. Claims, envelopes and signatures are not rewritten or appended by these repairs.

schema.detail: No DDL or storage version change. Local meta records person_cancellation_projection_rules=1 and resource_observations_version=3 atomically with successful projection repair. Startup refolding suppresses local completion-observation publication; projection tables, their digest/health state and existing lease overlays retain their usual rebuild behavior.

rules.detail: No checkpoint retention, claim schema or digest-column changes. Resource observations and step runs remain shared comparable projections, not host-local exemptions.

compatibility.detail: Roll the corrected build to every replica; an older binary can retain or recreate stale materializations. No client protocol or identity changes.

downtime.detail: The normal daemon restart performs a synchronous transactional one-time repair. Cancellation discovery uses kind/subject indexes and refolds selected run closures rather than the whole claim log. Resource version upgrade refreshes every retained observation/item-state subject and rebuilds preparation, so its cost scales with resource history (not just row count). Large-store startup duration has not been measured.

manual.detail: No explicit replay or repair command is required after deployment: each persistent store repairs at its next open. Set ST3_PROJECTION_MIGRATION_TIMING=1 and enable info-level tracing to log each migration's elapsed_ms on its first open. Operators must separately authorize any daemon rollout/restart.

recovery.detail: A failed opening transaction rolls back both repair and markers. Missing historical origins and explicitly degraded aggregates are counted and warned about once without blocking the completion marker; their existing health state remains. Other errors, including contention and deadlines, propagate rather than being marked complete. Unchanged subsequent opens skip completed repairs. A binary downgrade does not undo corrected projections and is not a convergence repair.
